- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially after recent spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >72.5), model often overshoots and fails to correct quickly; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% relative to prior day’s model output.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early 30-day forecasts — overcorrects after volatility; use 3–5 day smoothing filter on historical mean.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model tends to forecast flat or slightly upward; if true outcome shows divergence, add 1–3% downward adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid assuming linear decay — price often rebounds after 10–15 days; model underestimates recovery; add 2–5% upward bias in mid-horizon (days 10–20).
- If sentiment history shows repeated “1.00” (strong bullish) followed by “0.00” (neutral), model often fails to adjust — expect price to drop after 5–7 days; reduce forecast by 3–6% in next 5 days.
